c01s03.title: Three questions about one missed detail
items: What had to be noticed and remembered?
c01s03.caption: These are overlapping perspectives, not three competing descriptions of different people.

c01s03b.title: Observe a signal; examine the inference
c01s03b.caption: A brain image is a measurement with a comparison, not a direct label for a person’s thoughts.

c01s04.title: From explanation to a useful test
items: A change with an appropriate alternative
c01s04.caption: The goal is better decisions, not a more impressive-sounding label.

c01s05.title: Keep three statements separate
items: What change and useful outcome follow?
c01s05.caption: A persuasive story is not yet evidence for each link.

c02s03.title: Make the next action inspectable
items: Use memory or an accessible external cue
Apply the rule and check the result
c02s03.caption: An external aid changes the task demand; it is not evidence of a weaker person.

c02s03b.title: A return needs a place
c02s03b.caption: Reducing optional switching can help a specified task without requiring constant uninterrupted work.

c02s04.title: Ask about more than confidence
items: How does the person describe this shift?
What demands and recovery opportunities differed?
c02s04.caption: A state hypothesis is a reason to investigate conditions, not an individual diagnosis.

c02s05.title: A useful attention support
items: Define the step and meaningful result
Change one feasible demand or cue
Accuracy, effort, access and other differences
c02s05.caption: A quieter-looking task is not automatically a more successful one.

c03s03.title: Different evidence for different learning
c03s03.caption: Success in one memory demand does not establish success in every other demand.

c03s03b.title: Three different claims
items: Performance on the trained task changes
c03s03b.caption: Evidence for one claim does not automatically establish the others.

c03s04.title: Attempt, check and return
items: Explain or perform before seeing the answer
Use a trustworthy source or result
Try later and include a new example
c03s04.caption: A feasible learning cycle should target the capability you want to use.

c03s05.title: Choose a check that matches the claim
items: Can I do what I practised?
Can I explain and correct the idea?
Can I use it on a relevant unfamiliar case?
c03s05.caption: Different claims call for different checks; confidence alone is not all three.

c04s03.title: A learning signal; a much broader claim
right: Phone checking has several possible influences
Do not read a chemical level from it
c04s03.caption: A scientific term cannot replace the missing observation and comparison.

c04s03b.title: Investigate the routine
items: What else enables or blocks the intended action?
c04s03b.caption: A useful habit explanation includes the setting and competing goals.

c04s04.title: Prepare a feasible next action
items: What outcome matters to the person?
Are time, access and the next step available?
At this cue, take this concrete action
What happened and what did it cost?
c04s04.caption: A specific plan helps only if its situation and action are workable.

c04s05.title: A mechanism should improve a practical question
items: A response in a particular setting
c04s05.caption: A personal trial can inform a choice without diagnosing a chemical state.

c05s03.title: Separate the parts of the account
items: A higher pulse and a sharp reply
What did the situation mean to Jo?
Which practical or personal response fits?
c05s03.caption: No single physiological observation identifies another person’s emotion.

c05s03b.title: Different responses address different problems
c05s03b.caption: A personal skill and an environmental change can complement one another.

c05s04.title: Make room for recovery
items: What is being required, and for how long?
Can the person rest or obtain support?
Choose a feasible change in the arrangement
c05s04.caption: Recovery should not depend on meeting a productivity score first.

c05s05.title: Match the response to the difficulty
items: Ask what the situation means to the person
Change an identified demand or access problem
Use an optional strategy that fits
Consider rest, support and what remains difficult
c05s05.caption: A calmer feeling is one outcome; it is not the whole explanation or every practical goal.

c06s03.title: Prepare, pause and return
items: State the problem and what you tried
Test the idea against the actual requirements
c06s03.caption: A break is one part of a learning and checking cycle.

c06s03b.title: Generate; then judge the result
left: What different layouts could we try?
c06s03b.caption: A larger idea count is not automatically a better final solution.

c06s04.title: Ask what the practical evidence shows
items: Which processes or networks are proposed?
Does the setting and cost fit this person?
c06s04.caption: A neural explanation can guide questions without establishing the intervention’s benefit.

c06s05.title: Judge a useful change
items: What happened and what else differed?
Keep, adapt or stop with uncertainty visible
c06s05.caption: Understanding a mechanism and improving an everyday outcome remain connected but distinct tasks.
